newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Rugby Union-McKenna at full-back for Leinster.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-McKenna at full-back for Leinster.

text.p: Leinster on Friday named Peter McKenna at full-back on the team to meet French side Pau in Pool B of the European Cup at Lansdowne Road on Saturday (kick-off 1430 GMT).
The Old Belvedere player fills the berth which had been left vacant when the rest of the side was named earlier this week.
McKenna comes in for Ciaran Clarke who injured a hamstring in the 34-25 defeat of Scottish Borders last weekend.
Leinster go into Saturday's tie with two points from three games and are out of contention for a quarter-final place.
Pau made just one change to their side which lost 19-14 to Leicester of England last week, Thierry Mentieres coming into the second-row for Alain Lagouarde.

The French have two points from three games played to date but with a vastly superior scoring aggregate than Leinster, they can still go through to the quarter-finals should they win and Llanelli of Wales lose to table-leaders Leicester of England.
Ulster have made one change to the side defeated by Neath last weekend for their Pool C meeting with Brive of France at Ravenhill, Belfast, on Saturday.
Irish international Paddy Johns, who was not released by his club Saracens for the Neath game, returns to the second-row in place of Gary Longwell.

Ulster, with two points from three games, will be hoping that Brive, who are unbeaten on six points and have already qualified for the quarter-finals, will adopt a laissez-faire attitude going into the tie.

Even if Ulster do beat Brive, they will still need bottom of the table Scottish Caledonia to cause a huge upset and beat England's Harlequins if they are to advance to the latter stages of the competition.
Of three provincial side involved in the European Cup, Munster have the best chance of making the quarter-finals.
They travel to play Toulouse in France on Saturday knowing that a draw will be enough to push them through as runners-up in Pool D behind Welsh side Cardiff.

Toulouse are unlikely to finalise their side before Saturday, their most serious worry concerns international centre Thomas Castaignede who injured an ankle and went off the field in the 77-17 defeat by England's Wasps last weekend.
Elsewhere, Connacht made nine changes, two positional, to the team that lost to Toulon in France last weekend for their European Conference game at home to Orrell on Saturday.
